packet.headline_seed: Ghana delays visit by South African president amid row over anti-migrant protests
packet.description_seed: Many in Ghana feared his presence would lead to mass protests, and officials say it is postponed for now.

what: Ghana delays visit by South African president amid row over anti-migrant protests

clean_source_blocks.text: President Cyril Ramaphosa was due to fly to Ghana next month Ghana has postponed a visit by South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa following xenophobic rallies that resulted in hundreds of Ghanaians being repatriated from his country. Ramaphosa had long planned a state visit to Ghana in the first week of August, and it had been hoped this would help de-escalate tensions between the two nations. But many in Ghana feared his presence would lead to mass protests there. On Tuesday, government spokesman Felix Kwakye Ofosu told the BBC the visit would not happen for the time being. ''We sent them a communication indicating that it would be best to defer the visit in view of the present climate around xenophobia," he explained.
Many in Ghana feared his presence would lead to mass protests, and officials say it is postponed for now.

Other African countries - including Nigeria, Malawi and Kenya - have also been repatriating their nationals from South Africa because of ongoing protests against foreigners. Some groups gave undocumented migrants a deadline of 30 June to leave the country and about 25,000 have been repatriated so far. Ramaphosa has said that people have a right to protest as long as they were peaceful. He also said he would do more to tackle irregular migration. Anti-foreigner protests have led to thousands of people fleeing South Africa for their home countries elsewhere on the continent The row escalated last week when Ghana condemned the alleged killing of Bahiru Isak, a 40-year-old Ghanaian national living in the Khayelitsha suburb of Cape Town in South Africa. Ghanaian officials said he was killed during anti-immigration protests on 30 June. South Afric

South Africa has sought to play things down, with presidential spokesman Vincent Magwenya telling the BBC of the country's unwavering commitment to "deepening cooperation" between the "two sister nations" and "advancing the African Agenda". "The two countries will continue to engage through diplomatic channels to identify a mutually convenient date," he said. 'They came with machetes' - deadline looms for migrants to leave South Africa 'We have to prioritise South Africans': Anti-migrant movement blocks foreigners from healthcare Diplomatic tensions between the two nations heightened after a video went viral of Emmanuel Asamoah, a young Ghanaian living in South Africa, being confronted and told to ''go fix his country''. Ghana has since repatriated more than 900 of its citizens from South Africa, and the last batch of over 900 others is expected to be brought home in the coming weeks.

[Lähde: BBC World]
President Cyril Ramaphosa was due to fly to Ghana next month

Ghana has postponed  a visit by South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa following xenophobic rallies that resulted in hundreds of Ghanaians being repatriated from his country.

Ramaphosa had long planned a state visit to Ghana in the first week of August, and it had been hoped this would help de-escalate tensions between the two nations.

But many in Ghana feared his presence would lead to mass protests there. On Tuesday, government spokesman Felix Kwakye Ofosu told the BBC the visit would not happen for the time being.

"The two countries will continue to engage through diplomatic channels to identify a mutually convenient date," he said.

'They came with machetes' - deadline looms for migrants to leave South Africa

'We have to prioritise South Africans': Anti-migrant movement blocks foreigners from healthcare

Diplomatic tensions between the two nations heightened after a video went viral of Emmanuel Asamoah, a young Ghanaian living in South Africa, being confronted and told to ''go fix his country''.

Ghana has since repatriated more than 900 of its citizens from South Africa, and the last batch of over 900 others is expected to be brought home in the coming weeks.

Other African countries - including Nigeria, Malawi and Kenya - have also been repatriating their nationals from South Africa because of ongoing protests against foreigners. Some groups gave undocumented migrants a deadline of 30 June to leave the country and about 25,000 have been repatriated so far.

Ramaphosa has said that people have a right to protest as long as they were peaceful. He also said he would do more to tackle irregular migration.

Anti-foreigner protests have led to thousands of people fleeing South Africa for their home countries elsewhere on the continent

The row escalated last week when Ghana condemned the alleged killing of Bahiru Isak, a 40-year-old Ghanaian national living in the Khayelitsha suburb of Cape Town in South Africa. Ghanaian officials said he was killed during anti-immigration protests on 30 June.

South Afric

payload.title: Ghana lykkää Etelä-Afrikan presidentin vierailua siirtolaiskiistan keskellä
payload.summary: Ghana on lykännyt Etelä-Afrikan presidentin Cyril Ramaphosan suunniteltua valtiovierailua, koska Etelä-Afrikan ulkomaalaisvastaiset protestit ovat kiristäneet maiden välejä ja johtaneet ghanalaisten kotiuttamisiin.
payload.content:
Ghana on lykännyt Etelä-Afrikan presidentin Cyril Ramaphosan valtiovierailua tilanteessa, jossa Etelä-Afrikan ulkomaalaisvastaiset protestit ovat johtaneet ghanalaisten kotiuttamisiin ja kasvattaneet diplomaattista jännitettä maiden välillä. Ramaphosan oli määrä matkustaa Ghanaan elokuun ensimmäisellä viikolla, mutta Ghanassa pelättiin vierailun voivan laukaista laajoja mielenosoituksia.

## Vierailu siirtyy myöhemmäksi

Ghanan hallituksen edustaja Felix Kwakye Ofosu sanoi tiistaina, ettei vierailu toteudu toistaiseksi. Hänen mukaansa Etelä-Afrikalle toimitettiin viesti, jossa todettiin, että vierailun lykkääminen olisi nykyisessä ulkomaalaisvihamieliseen ilmapiiriin liittyvässä tilanteessa paras ratkaisu.

Vierailua oli valmisteltu pitkään, ja sen toivottiin aiemmin auttavan maiden välisten jännitteiden lieventämisessä. Nyt arvio kääntyi päinvastaiseksi: Ramaphosan läsnäolon pelättiin lisäävän levottomuuksien riskiä Ghanassa.

## Protestit ovat johtaneet kotiuttamisiin

Etelä-Afrikassa käynnissä olevat ulkomaalaisvastaiset protestit ovat saaneet useita Afrikan maita kotiuttamaan kansalaisiaan. Myös Nigeria, Malawi ja Kenia ovat ryhtyneet vastaaviin toimiin. Joidenkin ryhmien kerrotaan asettaneen paperittomille siirtolaisille määräajan lähteä maasta 30. kesäkuuta mennessä, ja tähän mennessä noin 25 000 ihmistä on kotiutettu.

Ramaphosa on sanonut, että ihmisillä on oikeus osoittaa mieltään, kunhan protestit pysyvät rauhanomaisina. Hän on myös sanonut aikovansa tehdä enemmän sääntöjenvastaisen maahanmuuton torjumiseksi.

## Diplomaattiset jännitteet jatkuvat

Ghanan ja Etelä-Afrikan välinen kiista kärjistyi viime viikolla, kun Ghana tuomitsi 40-vuotiaan ghanalaisen Bahiru Isakin väitetyn surman Kapkaupungin Khayelitshan alueella. Ghanalaisviranomaisten mukaan hänet tapettiin maahanmuuttovastaisten protestien aikana 30. kesäkuuta.

Jännitteitä on lisännyt myös video, jolla Etelä-Afrikassa asuva nuori ghanalainen Emmanuel Asamoah joutuu kohtaamisen kohteeksi ja häntä kehotetaan palaamaan korjaamaan omaa maataan. Etelä-Afrikka on pyrkinyt rauhoittamaan tilannetta. Presidentin tiedottaja Vincent Magwenya sanoi maan olevan sitoutunut syventämään yhteistyötä Ghanan kanssa ja edistämään Afrikan yhteistä agendaa.

Magwenyan mukaan maat jatkavat yhteydenpitoa diplomaattisia kanavia pitkin, jotta vierailulle voidaan löytää molemmille sopiva uusi ajankohta. Ghana on jo kotiuttanut Etelä-Afrikasta yli 900 kansalaistaan, ja toisen yli 900 hengen ryhmän odotetaan palaavan lähiviikkoina.
summary_bullets: Ghana on lykännyt Cyril Ramaphosan elokuulle suunniteltua valtiovierailua.
Päätöksen taustalla ovat Etelä-Afrikan ulkomaalaisvastaiset protestit ja pelko vastamielenosoituksista Ghanassa.
Ghana on kotiuttanut Etelä-Afrikasta yli 900 kansalaistaan, ja lisää paluukuljetuksia odotetaan lähiviikkoina.
